🗓️ Weekly recap (Oct 31-Nov 7) for Copilot CLI
🚀 2 releases
🛠️ 1274 improvements

1274 features & enhancements in this release

Top features:
• Rex terminals render inline images using Kitty direct placements 🖼️
• Add /code command to open the current session in VS Code
• Introduce Fusion tier setting to copilot config
• Make /settings open unified dashboard for all users + add global search across settings and local resources 🔍
• Interactive CLI reports program status to terminals, including attention-needed alerts ⚠️
• Add opt-in session management tools and mentions for opted-in local sessions
• Add GPT-6.1 Terra as selectable model under New models when available
• Add Sandbox extensions setting to run extension processes inside sandbox
• Add COPILOT_SESSION_CWD for launching and expanding LSP and local MCP server configs

Enhancements:
• MATS telemetry added for Entra authentication through OneAuth, respecting telemetry opt-out
• Improved prompt editing: images removed with Ctrl+U/K/W not sent in message; Ctrl+S can stash prompt
• Pasted text with Unicode separators now fills separate prompt lines; control characters dropped
• In -p --plan, agent no longer suggests Shift+Tab; asked to include plan key points in reply
• copilot --resume no longer waits indefinitely when task service unresponsive; timeout after 10s
• Sandboxed grep, rg, glob report Windows launch failures instead of silent no-match
• Model picker shows context window size for flat, unpriced, and single-tier models
• Sandboxed local MCP servers respect relative filesystem permissions even with different working directory
• PowerShell commands work on Windows with CLI in long directory paths
• MCP Entra auth falls back to VS Code registration when Copilot CLI preauthorization unavailable
• Sandboxed local MCP servers start correctly when configured with relative cwd
• On Windows, sandboxed sessions in nested Git dirs can change to and write at repo root
• Autopilot no longer triggers recommendations after review or analysis-only requests
• Suppress unnecessary MCP reload summaries when plugin servers remain unchanged
• Retries empty 404 responses from Copilot's service under load instead of failing turn
• copilot help config now lists all settings catalog offers, including previously missing settings
• ACP clients can switch --yolo sessions out of autopilot without blocking or policy issues
• The file picker now underlines matches in names with decomposed accents or capital dotted I correctly
• Up and Down keys in multi-line prompt keep column position when moving over shorter lines
• Ctrl+Y and /share research skip unreadable research folder entries instead of failing

Bug fixes:
• Switching sessions while other sessions busy no longer crashes CLI or leaves blank terminal
• Retain readable image attachments when retrying prompt with corrupt image
• Suppress sending removed or replaced images within edited prompt messages
• Fix bug where MCP reload summaries appeared unnecessarily
• copilot --resume stop waiting indefinitely on unresponsive tasks; now times out
• Windows sandboxed sessions handle nested Git repos correctly for file writes
• Fix crash issues when switching sessions with concurrent activity
• File picker no longer shortens matched folder rows for accented folders or special characters
• Fix prompt paste dropping trailing characters on handling control characters
• Prevent autopilot from starting implementation after simple review requests

Misc:
• Added MATS telemetry for Entra authentication respecting client opt-out
• Updated help config command to fully list all available configuration settings
• Improved CLI documentation on new configuration options and telemetry policies
• Enhanced internal logging of session management and task service failures

8 AI model architectures, visually explained:

LLMs get so much attention that it's easy to overlook the rest of the field. Different inputs, tasks, and deployment constraints have led to very different model designs.

Here are eight specialized AI model architectures:

1. LLM (Large language models)

Text is split into tokens, mapped to embeddings, and processed through transformer layers. The model generates its response by predicting successive tokens.

↳ GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama.

2. LCM (Large concept models)

Moves prediction to the sentence level. Sentences become SONAR embeddings, and the model predicts the next sentence representation. Meta explored both autoregressive and diffusion-based versions.

↳ Meta's LCM research introduced this approach.

3. LAM (Large action models)

Connects a user's request to actions in an environment. These systems interpret intent, plan steps, and use interfaces or tools, often checking results before continuing.

↳ Rabbit R1, Microsoft UFO, Claude Computer Use.

4. MoE (Mixture of experts)

A router assigns token representations to selected expert networks inside the model. Activating a subset of experts adds model capacity without running every expert for every token.

↳ Mixtral, DeepSeek, Switch Transformer.

5. VLM (Vision-language models)

Combines visual representations with language processing. A vision encoder extracts image features, which are connected to a language model so it can answer questions about visual content.

↳ GPT-4V, Gemini, LLaVA.

6. SLM (Small language models)

Uses fewer parameters to reduce memory and compute requirements. These models can run locally, with quantization often reducing their deployment footprint further.

↳ Phi-3, Gemma, Mistral 7B, Llama 3.2 1B.

7. MLM (Masked language models)

Learns by predicting hidden tokens using context on both sides. This bidirectional training produces representations useful for retrieval, classification, and other language-understanding tasks.

↳ BERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTa.

8. SAM (Segment Anything Model)

An image encoder processes the image, while a prompt encoder handles points, boxes, or masks. A mask decoder combines them to identify the requested regions.

↳ Meta's SAM supports interactive segmentation and image annotation.

These aren't eight mutually exclusive categories. A small model can process images, and a language model can use MoE layers. Some labels describe architecture, while others describe training or intended use.

There's another approach I kept outside the image because it alters how a model handles context rather than introducing a separate model family.

Recursive language models, from MIT, put the input into a Python environment that a root model can inspect through code.

The model can search or slice that input, then make recursive model calls on selected portions instead of loading everything into its own context window.

The reported experiments handled inputs beyond 10 million tokens without retraining, with gains over the base model even on some tasks whose inputs already fit its context window.

I recently wrote a full breakdown of how this works, including why accessing a large input and reasoning reliably over it are different problems.

Read it below.

I just had @bot call my phone and had a conversation with it. I asked about its capabilities, who created it, I had it tell me a story, and what about the voice assistant I can change.

Through the voice assistant it looks like I could request any changes or kick off any job by asking it to do so. I didn't try this, but that feels like a potential attack vector to me. I hope it's accounted for. You could have some one tell your virtual assistant to do kick off any task, so hopefully not the case.

Bot couldn't tell me who created it, just that it was powered by Grok. Sorry @poteto .

I figured I'd ask it to tell me a story and it started down this tale it wove but then I realized this is burning tokens so I stopped it.

Finally, I asked if I could have it not identify itself as a virutal assistant when making calls on my behalf. Bot told me that it was not allowed to change that initial greeting but could change anything beyond the self-identification.

I asked if Bot could change it's voice type and it could not. It sounds very AI in the voicetone but I suspect that is to further identify it as a virtual caller and not a real person.
